items.title: Standing Wave Ratio
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the ratio of maximum to minimum voltage along a feed line, caused by reflection from a mismatched load. a perfectly matched line shows 1:1. vswr voltage standing wave ratio

items.title: Reflection Coefficient
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the fraction of an incident wave's voltage that is reflected by a mismatched load, from 0 (perfect match) to 1 (total reflection).

items.title: Return Loss
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the reflected power expressed in decibels below the forward power. higher return loss means a better match — the opposite direction from swr.

items.title: Feed Line
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the cable carrying rf between transmitter and antenna, characterised by its impedance, loss per unit length, and velocity factor. transmission line coax coaxial cable ladder line

items.title: Characteristic Impedance
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the impedance a transmission line presents to a wave travelling along it, set by the line's geometry and dielectric — not by its length.

items.title: Velocity Factor
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the speed of a signal in a feed line as a fraction of its speed in free space, typically 0.66 for solid-dielectric coax and up to 0.95 for open-wire line.

items.title: Antenna Gain
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: how much more strongly an antenna radiates in its favoured direction than a reference antenna — dbi against an isotropic radiator, dbd against a half-wave dipole.

items.title: Effective Radiated Power
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: transmitter power adjusted for feed-line loss and antenna gain — what the antenna effectively radiates in its favoured direction, referenced to a dipole (erp) or an isotropic radiator (eirp). eirp

items.title: Voltage
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the difference in electrical potential between two points — the pressure that pushes charge around a circuit. always measured between two points, never at one. electromotive force emf potential difference v

items.title: Current
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the rate at which charge flows past a point in a circuit, measured in amperes. one ampere is one coulomb per second. amperage i

items.title: Resistance
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: opposition to current flow that converts electrical energy into heat, measured in ohms. unlike reactance, it dissipates power rather than storing and returning it.

items.title: Conductance
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the reciprocal of resistance, measured in siemens. handy for parallel circuits, where conductances simply add.

items.title: Power
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the rate of energy transfer, measured in watts. in a dc circuit it is simply voltage times current.

items.title: Peak Envelope Power
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the average power supplied during one complete rf cycle at the crest of the modulation envelope. it is the measure the fcc uses to set amateur power limits.

items.title: Impedance
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: total opposition to alternating current, combining resistance and reactance. because reactance shifts phase, impedance has both a magnitude and an angle.

items.title: Reactance
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: opposition to alternating current from capacitance or inductance. it stores energy and returns it rather than dissipating it as heat, and it changes with frequency.

items.title: Capacitance
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the ability to store energy in an electric field between conductors, measured in farads. a capacitor opposes a change in voltage.

items.title: Inductance
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the ability to store energy in a magnetic field around a conductor, measured in henries. an inductor opposes a change in current.

items.title: Resonance
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the frequency at which inductive and capacitive reactance are equal and cancel, leaving a purely resistive impedance.

items.title: Root Mean Square
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the equivalent dc value of an ac waveform — the value that would produce the same heating in a resistor. for a sine wave, rms = 0.707 x peak.

items.title: Peak Voltage
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the maximum instantaneous voltage a waveform reaches, measured from the zero line to the crest.

items.title: Peak-to-Peak Voltage
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the full swing of a waveform from its most negative to its most positive point — for a symmetrical wave, twice the peak voltage.

items.title: Decibel
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: a logarithmic unit expressing the ratio between two powers, voltages, or currents. it is always a ratio — never an absolute quantity — unless a reference is attached, as in dbm or dbw.

items.title: Frequency
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the number of complete cycles per second of a periodic signal, measured in hertz.

items.title: Wavelength
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the physical distance a radio wave travels during one complete cycle. inversely proportional to frequency.

items.title: Main Channel
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: in gmrs, one of the 16 channels at 462 or 467 mhz on 25 khz spacing that carry the highest power limits and, at 467 mhz, serve as repeater inputs.

items.title: Interstitial Channel
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: in gmrs, one of the 14 channels sitting halfway between the main channels, sharply limited in power and, at 467 mhz, restricted to hand-held units.

items.title: GMRS Repeater
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: a station that receives on a 467 mhz main channel and simultaneously retransmits on the paired 462 mhz main channel 5.000 mhz below, extending the range of hand-held and mobile stations.

items.title: Repeater Offset
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the fixed frequency difference between a repeater's input and output. gmrs uses +5.000 mhz; the 2 metre amateur band conventionally uses ±600 khz and 70 cm ±5 mhz. split shift duplex offset

items.title: Continuous Tone-Coded Squelch System
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: a sub-audible tone transmitted alongside speech that keeps a receiver's squelch closed unless the matching tone is present. pl privacy tone tone squelch subaudible tone

items.title: Digital Coded Squelch
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: a digital equivalent of ctcss: a continuous low-rate data pattern that a receiver checks before opening its squelch. same purpose, same non-privacy, different encoding. dpl digital privacy code

items.title: Family Radio Service
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: an unlicensed personal radio service sharing all 22 channel frequencies with gmrs, limited to 2 w erp on most channels, 0.5 w on channels 8-14, and permanently attached antennas.

items.title: Multi-Use Radio Service
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: an unlicensed service of five vhf channels near 151 and 154 mhz, limited to 2 w transmitter output, with repeaters prohibited but external antennas allowed.

items.title: Equipment Certification
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: fcc approval of a transmitter type for a specific radio service. part 95 services require it; the amateur radio service largely does not. type acceptance type accepted part 95 certified

items.title: Station Identification
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: transmitting your assigned call sign so that transmissions can be attributed to a licensee. required in every licensed radio service, with the timing set by that service's rules.

items.title: Control Operator
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the licensed amateur designated by the station licensee as responsible for the emissions from a station. every transmission has one, and the privileges of their licence class set what the station may do.

items.title: Harmful Interference
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: interference that endangers the functioning of a radionavigation or other safety service, or that seriously degrades, obstructs, or repeatedly interrupts a radiocommunication service operating in accordance with the regulations.

items.title: Volunteer Examiner Coordinator (VEC)
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: an organisation that has entered into an agreement with the fcc to coordinate, prepare, and administer amateur operator licence examinations, and that accredits the individual volunteer examiners who run sessions. vec volunteer examiner coordinator

items.title: Telemetry
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: a one-way transmission of measurements at a distance from the measuring instrument.

items.title: Pecuniary Interest
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: a financial stake in the content of a communication. amateur stations may not transmit communications in which the control operator or their employer has one.

items.title: Duty Cycle
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the percentage of time a transmitter is actually transmitting at full power during a defined averaging period.

items.title: Maximum Permissible Exposure
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: the fcc's limit on human exposure to radiofrequency fields, expressed as power density or field strength, varying with frequency and with whether the exposure is controlled or uncontrolled.

items.title: Non-Ionizing Radiation
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: electromagnetic radiation without enough energy per photon to strip electrons from atoms. radio signals, including every amateur and gmrs transmission, are non-ionizing.

items.title: Ionizing Radiation
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: radiation energetic enough to remove electrons from atoms, such as x-rays, gamma rays, and the emissions of radioactive decay.

items.title: RF Burn
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: a skin burn caused by touching a conductor carrying radio-frequency current — typically an antenna element while transmitting.

items.title: Lightning Arrester
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: a device in a feed line that shunts high-voltage surges to ground, installed on a grounded panel where feed lines enter the building. surge protector coax arrester

items.title: Bonding
items.subtitle: Term
items.keywords: connecting all ground rods, equipment grounds, and the electrical service ground together with heavy conductor, so no potential difference can develop between them.
